writeup.headline: Alphabet rates Hold: strong growth and a net-cash balance sheet offset by a high valuation and weak trend.
writeup.thesis: Alphabet scores 58, a Hold, 7 points short of Buy. The business side is strong: TTM revenue growth of 20.1%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 24.2% year on year, and growth sped up by 2.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is solid, with a 33.1% operating margin, and the balance sheet scores 100 thanks to net cash and cash at 2.42 times debt. Valuation holds the score back at 24: in absolute terms P/S of 8.8x and P/FCF of 74.1x are high, with the FCF yield 3.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is rated expensive overall, with P/FCF more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends. The trend score of 42 is also a drag, with the price 20.4% below its 52-week high and shares 17.3 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: High absolute valuation, with P/FCF of 74.1x and a free cash flow margin of only 11.9% as heavy AI spending absorbs cash
Ongoing antitrust and regulatory pressure in the US, EU and South Korea, plus a pending securities class action
Weak price trend: price 6.0% below its 200-day average and lagging both SPY and QQQ
Reliance on large AI cloud counterparties such as Anthropic
Mixed reception of Q3 results, with EPS down year over year and analyst target changes split
what_would_change: A 7-point score gain would reach Buy, for example from a recovering price trend or a better valuation score after a pullback or stronger free cash flow
Positive post-earnings guidance or analyst upgrades lifting the news risk score above its current 50
A 14-point drop would mean Sell, which would likely need slowing growth together with a further fall in the trend score or adverse regulatory rulings
